articles.title: Dan’s Daily: Trade Demands Fizzling; Penguins Clean Up
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins played a professional, clean game Saturday, which might not normally make headlines, but after the last 10 […]
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Penguins played a professional, clean game Saturday, which might not normally make headlines, but after the last 10 periods, the choir of angels sang, and the rainbox arched the arena. The Penguins beat the Dallas Stars in a shootout, but it was how they got there that was the story, and we've got the inside analysis. Elsewhere in the Daily, the fallout is just beginning in New York, where super goalie Igor Shesterkin is out for the year.

Also, the NHL trade rumors are beginning to turn from interested teams to staying put as the players who have demanded out confront the possibility that no trade is coming. But leave it to Montreal, which tried to change that for Dylan Larkin Saturday. Those glorious hockey-loving fans chanted, "We Want Larkin!" as the Montreal Canadiens beat the Detroit Red Wings.

I didn't write about this last night. I gave it only a passing reference, but the win over Dallas cannot be overstated. This season was beginning to teeter, and another bad loss or two and they would have been in the swamp. The Penguins are far from out of the woods, but simply not beating themselves to a pulp worked wonders.

But they always play well against the larger Dallas team that doesn't play a fast brand of hockey. They've got Chicago, Colorado, Vegas, and Utah on the docket next…

If anybody wants to grab dinner at Herbs and Rye in Vegas, or Bautista's Hole in the Wall, I'm in.

Pittsburgh Hockey Now: Dan made a mistake Saturday and checked the wrong button, so this story was behind the paywall for a bit, but I wanted to make it a free PHN+ preview. It's free now—our weekly Penguins insider column. The conversations we have in the room, the chats away from the media scrums, and the vibes were getting. This week, we followed up on our deep conversation with Ville Koivunen from last season, and Evgeni Malkin interrupted a conversation to declare who he wants to play with, which is definitely a PHN exclusive. Check it out—the Penguins Room feature .

I hope many of you will come back to PHN+ now that the tech side is settled.

To the game, you can get the game synopsis and the goals breakdown here . In the report card, we dug into the Xs and Os of the contest, as well as the sad, but one immutable fact as coach Dan Muse made a couple of lineup tweaks that paid big…BIG dividends in the Penguins' win .

We also talked with Spencer Stastney after the game. Boy, he's a talker. And our postgame video. Now more concise!

NHL Trade Talk, News, & National Hockey Now

Montreal Hockey Now: We want Larkin! The fans chanted, and even Larkin was a little taken aback by the fans. What's the reality of the Montreal Canadiens' trade pursuit of Larkin?

HNIC: The Hockey Night in Canada Headlines Segment. Elliotte Friedman poo-pooed immediate speculation that the Rangers could chase Connor Hellebuyck following Igor Shesterkin's season-ending injury. Friedman also raised the possibility that a few players will remain with their teams, especially Alexander Nikishin .

NHLtraderumors.me: Friedman reported Detroit is still trying to keep Simon Edvinsson, but if they do trade him, perhaps that's the way they get the young center they want. There are four potential targets if Detroit can trade Edvinsson for a young pivot .

Philly Hockey Now: It's the middle of October, and the Philadelphia Flyers are getting worse, not better. Another–yes, another–bad loss, this time to the Boston Bruins. Our Will James has the locker room reactions and analysis from Boston. Those lovable Philly Flyers are frustrated.

Boston Hockey Now: The flip side is that the Boston Bruins are figuring it out. Jack Studley was there with good coverage of the Bruins' win .

Those two, Jack and Will, are going to be staples in this business for a long time. They're good and getting better. I'm proud to have them on the team.

Chicago Hockey Now: Frank Nazar is in timeout after his ugly hit on Bo Horvat drew a couple of game suspensions. Nazar faced the music and said he texted Horvat, too. It was a bad look for the Chicago Blackhawks forward.

articles.title: D.J. Moore: why fantasy managers should brace for "D.J. less"
articles.summary: Some teams' #1 WRs are secure atop the depth chart even when they're injured; That's not necessarily the case for D.J. Moore.
articles.body:
Some teams' #1 WRs are secure atop the depth chart even when they're injured; however long they're sidelined, these receivers will pick up where they left off. That's not necessarily the case for D.J. Moore, whose fantasy value is wobbly at best. Here's why fantasy managers should consider selling high.

Let's set the stage: Moore was a prized offseason acquisition for a Buffalo squad that needed a wideout boost. Last season, Khalil Shakir was a miscast #1, leading a group comprised of underperformer Keon Coleman, journeyman Joshua Palmer, Tyrell Shavers, and a smattering of post-prime pass catchers winding down their careers.

Compared to that group, Moore was a sizable upgrade. He then delivered big numbers in Week 1 and "sold" numbers in Week 3. Injuries limited him to only 23 offensive snaps in the Bills ' other two contests, where he caught only one pass on two targets.

Moore is not ascending. He was the Bears ' #1 WR in 2023, but by 2025 he was effectively their #3, stepping up only when Rome Odunze or Luther Burden got hurt. He'll turn 30 in April. Time isn't on his side, and neither is his current situation as an injured receiver in a corps that's getting better without him.

Essentially, when Moore finally returns to 100%, he'll be competing for targets with three guys, Shakir, Coleman, and Dalton Kincaid, who seem to have improved since last year and have, at various times this past month, looked like Josh Allen's favorite receiver.

Fantasy managers should be wary of Moore's rest-of-season value. The longer he's sidelined, the harder it will be for him to produce at a #1 WR level.

articles.title: The Giants’ pass rush just lost another body it couldn’t spare
articles.summary: The Giants placed Chauncey Golston on injured reserve Saturday, turning an already confirmed absence against Washington into a larger depth […]
articles.body:
The Giants placed Chauncey Golston on injured reserve Saturday , turning an already confirmed absence against Washington into a larger depth concern. With Brian Burns also on IR, this isn't a group with much room for another unavailable defensive lineman.

The team also announced standard practice-squad elevations for outside linebacker Trace Ford and receiver Dalen Cambre. Ford adds an option for Sunday's game, but his elevation doesn't establish a permanent roster spot or a full-time replacement for Golston.

The Giants still have to replace Golston's snaps

Golston hasn't recorded a sack this season, so nobody needs to exaggerate this into the loss of the team's leading pass rusher. He played in all four games, started twice and recorded 12 combined tackles. Taking another experienced player out of the rotation still leaves work that somebody has to handle.

That work includes getting through normal downs without exhausting the remaining rushers before an important third down. A defense can miss a rotation player even when his absence doesn't remove a big number from the sack column.

I'd be careful about treating every Ford appearance as a chance to send him after the quarterback. The first standard should be a clean assignment: maintain the edge, understand the call and avoid giving Washington an easy route outside because a young player chased pressure too aggressively. More responsibility can follow reliable snaps.

An elevation helps, but it doesn't settle the rotation

Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux remain active options on the outside. The coaching staff can ask more of established players, but asking them to carry every important snap is a different plan from having useful relief available.

The alternative is a tighter rotation, with the most trusted players handling the difficult situations and Ford contributing selectively. That might be the right approach Sunday. It also makes efficiency on the earlier downs more important because extra possessions create extra work for an already reduced group.

There is no reported return date for Golston in the Saturday transaction announcement. His move to IR shouldn't be described as proof that his season is over, and Ford's elevation shouldn't be sold as a solution before he plays.

Sunday gives the Giants a chance to see which reserve assignments they can trust. That evaluation needs to be useful beyond this one game, because a healthy Burns-Golston rotation is no longer available to fall back on.

articles.title: What Happened to Saquon Barkley? Latest Update on Eagles Star’s Injury and Why He’s Not Playing in Week 5 vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: It has been a wild turnaround for the Philadelphia Eagles over the last week. After a 2-0 start, it seemed like things were getting back on track following a...
articles.body:
It has been a wild turnaround for the Philadelphia Eagles over the last week. After a 2-0 start, it seemed like things were getting back on track following a disappointing 2025 campaign. But since then, it's gone a bit downhill.

However, it could get worse before it gets better as they take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5 for their international game scheduled in London. Saquon Barkley, however, will play no part in the proceedings.

The decision to bring Barkley to town proved to be instantly beneficial for the Eagles. Setting the all-time single-season record for rushing yards (regular season and playoffs combined) was critical en route to the franchise's second Super Bowl championship.

Since then, though, the returns have been diminishing. After a mediocre 2025 season, he made a slow start this year, tallying 182 rushing yards in four games, though he left the last game against the Rams after just two carries. He will not get a chance to add to that tally in Week 5.

After suffering a hamstring injury against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4, he was unable to practice throughout the week. As a result, he has been ruled out for their game in London.

Eagles' Outlook After Saquon Barkley's Injury

Losing a game to the Chicago Bears, who were starting Case Keenum at quarterback, was the start of this string of bad luck for the Eagles. They followed up that disaster by blowing a 10-point lead to the Rams in the final eight minutes of the game.

Moreover, Jalen Hurts finished with 93 passing yards on 27 attempts in that game, one of the worst performances of his career. But things took a turn for the worse over the course of the week.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Franchise legend Lane Johnson unexpectedly announced his retirement, leaving the Eagles without a key piece of their offensive line. Thereafter, in a move that many perceived as a sign that a fire sale might be in the works, they chose to trade Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens.

Now, as they face a red-hot Jaguars team, the offense appears to be in disarray. Alongside Barkley, backup running back Tank Bigsby was also placed on the injured reserve list, leaving the ground game in the hands of Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce. Carson Steele has also been elevated from the practice squad as insurance.

DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown have also been ruled out, leaving their wide receiver room shorthanded as well.

articles.title: Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard won't play vs. Jaguars in London because of ankle injury
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard won't play against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium because of an ankle inj...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard won't play against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium because of an ankle injury.

Greenard, injured in the third quarter against the Los Angeles Rams last week, did not practice this week and had been listed as questionable.

Philadelphia had previously ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), C Drew Kendall (knee), S Marcus Epps (groin) and WR Marquise Brown (ankle).

On Saturday, the Eagles elevated TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu.

For the Jaguars, S Eric Murray (concussion) won't play. He had been limited in practice. DB Jaylon Jones (hamstring) had been ruled out Friday.

The Jags' other inactives were: WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis.

On Saturday, Jacksonville signed LB Jalen McLeod to the active roster from the practice squad, elevated CB Jabbar Muhammad and S Kaevon Merriweather to the active roster from the practice squad, and waived LB Jack Kiser.

articles.title: Is Jayden Daniels playing today? Update on Commanders QB's injured elbow
articles.summary: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Week 2, but got positive news this week prior to facing the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels is officially back for the Washington Commanders , head coach Dan Quinn confirmed on Friday, Oct. 9.

Daniels dislocated his left elbow during the team's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. While many anticipated the injury – which was an aggravation of an injury he suffered during the 2025 campaign – would sideline Daniels long-term, the 25-year-old has made a speedy recovery.

Quinn was asked about the value of getting his starting QB back for a Week 5 game against the New York Giants .

"Command at the line, that's one for sure," Quinn said. "The play-making ability, the third and fourth downs, all of those are part of what makes him special in that way. Love the accuracy that he throws with and the good job obviously taking care of the ball. That's going to be premium in this game."

Here's what to know about Daniels' injury , his status and Washington's overall health at the quarterback position entering Week 5.

NFL Week 4 highlights, reactions and biggest moments around the league

Is Jayden Daniels playing against the Giants?

Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough effectively announced Daniels would be playing in Week 5 during a media availability on Thursday, Oct. 8.

"He's full go, man," Blough told reporters when asked about Daniels' status. "We're looking forward to having him back."

Daniels is expected to wear a brace on his non-throwing elbow to protect and stabilize it.

Daniels' return to the lineup won't be the only shake-up for Washington's quarterback depth chart. The Commanders also figure to have a new backup quarterback, as Marcus Mariota aggravated an MCL sprain in his Week 4 start against the Colts.

That will position seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis to move into the backup role behind Daniels. The Rutgers product played in relief of Mariota against the Colts, completing 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

"We've got a lot still to figure out roster-wise," was Quinn's reply on Friday when asked about the team's plan for Hartman.

articles.title: Todd McLellan Admits Red Wings’ Off-Ice Drama Has Become a Distraction
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings coach Todd McLellan admits Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson's ongoing situations have created distractions for his team.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings have enough challenges trying to win hockey games, but head coach Todd McLellan admitted Saturday night that the drama surrounding the organization has made his job even more difficult. Following Detroit's 1-0 shootout loss to the Montreal Canadiens, McLellan acknowledged that the ongoing uncertainty involving Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson has created a distraction for his team.

With the Red Wings off to a disappointing 1-3-1 start, McLellan is trying to keep his players focused on hockey while two major personnel situations continue to hang over the franchise.

Feb 28, 2026; Raleigh, North Carolina, USA; Detroit Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan looks on against the Carolina Hurricanes during the third period at Lenovo Center. Mandatory Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Todd McLellan Admits Red Wings Are Dealing With Distractions

Speaking to reporters following Saturday's game, McLellan acknowledged the challenge of keeping his team focused amid everything happening outside the locker room.

As reported by the Detroit Free Press , McLellan admitted:

"I'd be lying if I said everything going on wasn't a distraction, but we have a responsibility to each other to focus on what we can control and that's what we do."

McLellan also credited the players, coaches, and training staff for supporting one another and remaining committed to preparing for games despite the uncertainty surrounding the organization.

The coach's frustration became even more apparent when the conversation continued to focus on Larkin. McLellan eventually made it clear that he was tired of repeatedly addressing the situation and did not want to discuss it further.

Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson Situations Continue to Loom Large

The Red Wings have spent the opening weeks of the season dealing with two significant storylines that have little to do with what happens on the ice. Larkin's offseason trade request remains unresolved, while Edvinsson's contract stalemate has left Detroit without one of its most important young defensemen.

Saturday's game provided another reminder of how difficult those distractions have become to escape. Canadiens fans repeatedly chanted "We want Larkin," turning Detroit's former captain into one of the biggest storylines of the night despite neither team scoring during regulation or overtime.

Despite the outside noise, McLellan's team delivered a much-improved defensive performance against Montreal. Goaltender Daniil Tarasov stopped all 30 shots he faced before the Red Wings ultimately fell in the shootout.

McLellan deserves credit for acknowledging the situation rather than pretending everything is business as usual. However, the reality is that neither the Larkin situation nor Edvinsson's contract uncertainty appears likely to disappear simply because the Red Wings want to focus on hockey.

Detroit has now lost four of its first five games, and another slow start is the last thing this franchise needs following 10 consecutive seasons without a playoff appearance. The challenge for McLellan is finding a way to keep his locker room united while the organization works through decisions that could significantly impact its future.

articles.title: OVC Preview Series: Lindenwood Lions
articles.summary: Kyle Gerdeman needed to replace everyone after having the school’s best season at Division I
articles.body:
It's always difficult to replace your best player. It's even more difficult when you're coming off the high of the first winning season your school has had since entering Division I. It's three times more difficult when everyone from that team is gone, and it's back to square one. All of these things happened to Kyle Gerdeman during the offseason.

Surrounding this Lions roster is a clear bit of uncertainty. With every single player from last year's team electing to move out or move on , the coaching staff looks to rely on a multitude of new faces for success this season.

"The focus was just on how we rebuild our entire roster, and there was one thing that really helped do that, and that's that we finally were able to solidify a style of play [last year]," Gerdeman said. "After three years of getting through the transition of recruiting, I thought last year we finally got to the style of play that we wanted on offense. We got to the style of play we wanted on defense, and for the first time, really, we were able to really target guys that we thought were talented and fit our style of play vs. just grabbing talented guys and trying to squeeze them in, and I think that was kind of our approach to recruiting, to the transfer portal, [and] to everything was 'Let's make sure now that we can find guys that really fit what we want to do on both ends of the floor.'"

On the offensive side of the floor, Xavier Spencer looks to make an immediate impact in St. Charles for Gerdeman. The 6-foot-1 floor general averaged 11.9 points on 33.8 minutes per game for UMass Lowell and started all 33 games last season for the Riverhawks.

"What we needed was obviously some experience, and I thought he had that," Gerdeman said. "He played a ton of minutes last year at Lowell, played a big role for them. I think he can play some one, and I think he can play off the ball, and then really, [for] what we're doing in the half court, he can kind of combo it up a little bit. I think Mekhi Cooper was a great point guard for us, and I think Xavier gives us a little bit of that also, but I think he also kind of gives us a guy that can score and do more things than just a true point guard."

Other than Spencer in the backcourt, Kellen Robinson looks to return from injury to play his first collegiate basketball game for the Lions. Coming off an ACL tear the year prior, Robinson is the younger brother of former All-OVC First Teamer KK Robinson (now at New Mexico State), who had a standout year for Little Rock in 2023-24 before falling to two years of injury troubles. The younger Robinson now looks to prevent the injury bug after transferring from the Trojans. He was a standout for Bryant High School prior to college and was ranked the No. 3 prospect in the state of Arkansas after being a part of two straight state championship teams.

"When you come across a guy like Kellen, who was a redshirt freshman down there last year at Little Rock, I think everybody knew his talent," Gerdeman said. "So you know, now he's having a guy with some experience come in to kind of stabilize him a little bit at Xavier, and he's a guy that's hungry to get back on the court and who's obviously super talented."

Behind Robinson and Spencer are a slew of other guards who will look to carve out minutes: Shamiere Green (Lee College), Dom Clay (North Dakota State), Miles White (Lipscomb) and Malek Archie, who joined the team midway through last season after transferring from Tarleton State.

In the frontcourt, Gerdeman brought in length to pad the inside in Fresno State and Stetson transfers Makhan Diouf and Matar Diop, both of whom look to find a larger role at Lindenwood.

"What you get with Makhan is a guy that can play all over the place," Gerdeman said. "He's got tremendous guard skills, beyond being a forward or a four or five, so to speak. He can kind of give you that versatile guy. Matar Diop, coming from Stetson, kind of gives you that bouncy rim protector, that rim runner, that dunker spot guy."

Also coming in from Arizona Western College is Marsai Mason, who looks to be similar to what the Lions got from Jadis Jones in the past. The 6-foot-6 big man averaged 16.7 points and 9.9 rebounds on 51.4% shooting last season at the JUCO level. He looks to be a staple in the lineup along with 6-foot-11 North Macedonian big man Marko Lukanoski, who might be the best replacement for the loss of senior Milos Nenadic from last season.

"At this level it's hard to find good bigs," Gerdeman said. "Here's a high school kid coming in that has a chance to play some minutes as a freshman and do some things. When you find guys like that, I think you got to try to grab them."

articles.title: NC State takes a walloping from Wake, 38-14
articles.summary: It’s occurred to me lately that college football games are simply too long. A whole hour? Feels excessive. What if we trimmed the games down by, oh, let’s sa...
articles.body:
It's occurred to me lately that college football games are simply too long. A whole hour? Feels excessive. What if we trimmed the games down by, oh, let's say 30 minutes—wouldn't we all be a lot happier with a tidy sports outing such as that? I have to think we would.

Anyway, if you missed it, you didn't really, because you've seen it a lot before: NC State got outplayed in the second half. The Pack watched a halftime lead quickly evaporate and the margin went zooming in the other direction from there. Neither the offense nor the defense showed for the last two quarters, as State was held scoreless while Wake Forest scored four touchdowns and only punted the ball once.

State didn't score in the second quarter, either, perhaps reaching for bold new frontiers in underwhelming efforts moving forward. Let's hope not. But the Pack's ground game was basically useless from the start—not a terrible shock under the circumstances—and when every down is a passing down, that's generally going to be a problem. Unless you have an elite passing game, which NC State obviously does not.

Wake created a lot more havoc plays than it is accustomed to, stuffing nearly half of State's rushing attempts. CJ Bailey didn't throw an interception but Wake did a good job containing the pass game and forcing State to sustain drives, which it could not. Bailey threw for 243 yards but averaged just 6.2 yards per attempt. When the other team doesn't have to give you rushing attack even an ounce of respect, it's going to create problems.

Wake's rushing game wasn't a whole lot better, but it was far more effective than State throwing the ball. Gio Lopez was playing easy pitch-and-catch out there, completing almost 79% of his attempts for an average of 9.2 yards per attempt. NC State's pass defense has allowed 8+ yards per attempt and 2+ passing touchdowns in four straight games, and that is quite bad. Big capital-p Problem right there.

State's got some extra time to think about all of this and maybe get slightly healthier before going to Stanford. There are a lot of things that no amount of extra film study is going to fix, and anyway I'm getting to a point where I'm not sure I care much one way or the other.

articles.title: Swiss Darts Trophy: Ross Smith vows 'karma' will catch up with Mensur Suljovic after Austrian encourages boos
articles.summary: Ross Smith has hit out at Mensur Suljovic on social media after the Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo his opponent at the Swiss Darts Trophy; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The two players were deadlocked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and give his opponent a chance at the match.

Suljovic then nailed a double 10 with his last dart to secure the checkout and the victory, although his unsportsmanlike antics left a sour taste in Smith's mouth, later taking to X to post his thoughts after the defeat.

"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.

"Obviously it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.

"If he wants to be an absolute helmet that's on him - karma will come around."

Suljovic is no stranger to controversial incidents. The Austrian denied intentionally provoking Joe Cullen during a World Championship clash last December.

Cullen described his pace of play as like "cheating" and "not darts" after 'The Rockstar' was unhappy with the length of time his opponent was taking to recover his darts and the time he was taking to celebrate - with referee Kirk Bevans even forced to intervene.

"I never, ever do this as a provocation," Suljovic said in his response to Cullen. "I do it only for my game.

"I like my game - I never do it to be a villain. Sorry Joe, I never do this - I love you man."

articles.title: Citroën resucita el 2 CV: eléctrico, pequeño y fabricado en Europa por 15.000 euros
articles.standfirst: El 2 CV Concept anticipa un nuevo modelo para 2028 que recupera la receta del original: sencillez, sentido práctico y un precio accesible. Hasta tiene un hueco para llevar huevos.
articles.summary: El 2 CV Concept anticipa un nuevo modelo para 2028 que recupera la receta del original: sencillez, sentido práctico y un precio accesible. Hasta tiene un hueco para llevar huevos.
articles.body: El Citroën 2 CV está de vuelta. De momento, como un prototipo, pero con algo más que la nostalgia de un modelo extremadamente popular en España y en su país de origen, Francia. Precisamente allí, en el marco del Salón del Automóvil de París, es donde va a volver a la vida. Este nuevo Citroën 2 CV representa el compromiso de la marca del chevron de un nuevo modelo eléctrico que presentará de aquí a 2028, fabricado en Europa (clave en un momento en el que la industria se está protegiendo de la 'invasión' china) y lo más importante: con un objetivo de precio de partida de unos 15.000 euros (aunque de momento Citroën no lo expresa como compromiso sino como meta). Una cifra que, si se cumple, podría convertir este argumento en algo más importante incluso que la nostalgia de su diseño. Se llama Citroën 2 CV Concept y su planteamiento recupera una idea que parece haber perdido terreno en el automóvil moderno: ofrecer lo necesario, prescindir de lo superfluo y hacer un coche pequeño que no necesite crecer en tamaño, peso y precio para resultar atractivo. El envoltorio, eso sí, juega con ventaja: pocos modelos tienen una silueta tan reconocible como la del 2 CV. El primer dato que nos llama la atención está en la cinta métrica. El nuevo concepto mide 3,76 metros de largo, por lo que, según destaca Citroën, es incluso más corto que el 2 CV original. Pero tiene sentido ya que con esa talla, el futuro modelo ocupará el espacio entre el AMI y el ë-C3 y estará concebido para encajar en la futura normativa europea E-Car, que quiere promover Europa para potenciar su industria. Citroën también apunta a un peso de alrededor de una tonelada, todo un objetivo ambicioso porque, no nos olvidemos, hablamos de un eléctrico. La lógica es sencilla: menos kilos permiten recurrir a una batería más pequeña y económica, dimensionada para los desplazamientos cotidianos. Por ahora, Citroën no ha anunciado capacidad de batería, autonomía ni potencia. La reinterpretación conserva los faros redondos separados de la carrocería, los pasos de rueda abombados y la característica caída del techo en la zaga. La forma en la que Citroën ha conseguido resolver el rostro del coche, dentro de un minimalismo extremo, nos ha gustado. No tanto la vista trasera... El 2 CV Concept adopta tecnología LED de iluminación y unas llamativas llantas de acero de 19 pulgadas, con un estilo retro totalmente buscado. Con el techo practicable de lona, Citroën recupera uno de los rasgos más recordados de su antecesor. Como también los paragolpes separados de la carrocería, que pueden sustituirse de forma independiente y aportan una solución pensada para facilitar las reparaciones. Las superficies planas y otros elementos del diseño responden igualmente a esa búsqueda de una sencillez industrial que ayude a abaratar su precio. Dentro, el prototipo sustituye el salpicadero tradicional por una estructura cilíndrica sobre la que se organizan los mandos y las pantallas. Hay un volante de un solo radio (guiño al original), una pantalla táctil cuadrada de ocho pulgadas (que los que condujeron uno en los 70 no podían ni soñar) y asientos con tecnología Citroën Advanced Comfort, (que pretenden lograr el confort que sí tenían los del ancestro). Va vestidos con una tapicería de cuadros amarillos que impacta a la vista (muy de concept) y añade una cesta extraíble que ocupa el lugar de la consola central y unas tiras flexibles sirven como tiradores de las puertas. El detalle más simpático quizá sea la ‘Radioën’, una radio desmontable que también funciona como altavoz fuera del coche. Aunque tiene competencia: los pedales muestran una tortuga en el freno y un conejo en el acelerador, y los huecos de las puertas están diseñados para alojar huevos, un guiño a las exigencias prácticas que dieron origen al 2 CV. Incluso los sonidos del arranque y del claxon evocan al clásico. ¿Cuánto de este 2 CV Concept sobrevivirá al paso a producción? Es probable que bastante, viendo sobre todo cómo a Renault le ha funcionado el concepto, especialmente con el R5. Debería estar en la gama de Citroën durante el año 2028... así que la espera aún va a ser algo larga.

articles.summary: It's a rainy day at MetLife Stadium and the wet weather has dampened the offenses for both the Jets and the Browns.
articles.body:
It's a rainy day at MetLife Stadium and the wet weather has dampened the offenses for both the Jets and the Browns.

The Jets opened the game with a brisk, 80-yard touchdown drive, but that was the only visit to the end zone for either team over the first 30 minutes of play. The Browns were able to pick up a pair of field goals and the Jets lead 7-6 with the ball coming their way to kick off the second half.

Jets quarterback Geno Smith connected with wide receiver Garrett Wilson three times for 70 yards and a touchdown on that opening drive, but the ball has only gone Wilson's way once since he found the end zone. That pass fell incomplete and Smith only has 25 yards on his other five completions. He's also been sacked three times with Browns defensive tackle Maliek Collins picking up a pair of them.

The Jets defense has kept the team in front despite that offensive struggle. First-round pick David Bailey has two of their four sacks of Deshaun Watson and the Browns have managed just 99 yards on their 33 offensive plays.

Wide receiver KC Concepcion left with a head injury in the first quarter and will not return, so the Browns will have to look elsewhere for someone to spark their offense in the second half.

articles.title: Ankle issue for TreVeyon Henderson
articles.summary: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson suffers ankle injury and is questionable to return
articles.body:
New England Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) suffered an ankle injury during the Week 5 game and is considered questionable to return.

Why It Matters: Fantasy players should monitor the situation to see how long Henderson may be sidelined. Rhamondre Stevenson will see most of the work at running back if Henderson misses time and can be a No. 2 or No. 3 running back in fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni takes blame for Eagles' collapse: 'I cost us that game'
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni said he alone is to blame for the Eagles' collapse after the coach's decision to keep a kickoff in bounds proved disastrous.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Siranni put the blame for his team's last-second collapse against the Jacksonville Jaguars solely on himself.

After the Jaguars returned a kickoff with 8 seconds left to set up kicker Cam Little for a 57-yard game-winning field goal as time expired, Sirianni said he alone bears responsibility for the outcome.

"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game," Sirianni said after the 19-17 defeat in London . "And that's what I told the guys."

NFL Week 5 highlights, standout performances and reactions

The Eagles took a one-point lead after the team's two-minute offense set up Jake Elliott for a 48-yard field goal.

Despite Jacksonville being out of timeouts, Sirianni instructed Elliott to keep the ensuing kickoff in bounds rather than booting it out of the end zone. Catching the ball at his 8-yard with a running start, Ameer Abdullah found a seam and ran the kick back 53 yards before he was dragged down by Jarrian Jones with one-second remaining.

Little, who set the NFL record for longest field goal a year earlier, converted the ensuing field goal with no trouble, setting off a wild celebration for the Jaguars.

"What hurts there is that the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game, and I cost us the game," Siranni said. "And I put that fully on me."

Philadelphia entered the international matchup significantly shorthanded yet again. Beyond the midweek retirement of offensive line linchpin Lane Johnson and the trade sending Cam Jurgens to Baltimore , a horde of key starters – including running back Saquon Barkley – were held out.

Yet despite being outgained 408-232 in total yards, the Eagles had been poised to emerge with a win after Elliott's kick. Instead, the outcome plunged the team to 2-3, marking the first time since 2021 – Sirianni's first season at the helm – that its record dipped below. 500.

Sirianni refused to detail the factors that drove his decision, but Elliott confirmed that he did as instructed.

"That's gotta be a question for (Sirianni)," Elliott told reporters when asked about the strategy. "He's got stipulations on exactly what the amount of time is. But it didn't work this time."

The loss marked the second time in as many weeks that the Eagles collapsed down the stretch, with a lengthier unraveling looming over their 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

articles.title: Steelers WR Situation Getting Dire? Another Leaves Game vs. Colts
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH — As the Pittsburgh Steelers tried to put up some points before halftime, receiver Roman Wilson exited the game […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — As the Pittsburgh Steelers tried to put up some points before halftime, receiver Roman Wilson exited the game and headed to the locker room.

Wilson, a third-year Michigan product, appeared to be holding his wrist after an 11-yard reception that was overturned before Chris Boswell nailed a 48-yard field goal to make it 17-13 with 21 seconds remaining in the first half.

That was Wilson's only target of the game to that point, with running back Jaylen Warren having taken a short pass 80 yards for a touchdown in the first quarter, then tight end Pat Freiermuth reeled in a one-yard score in the second.

At halftime, Warren is the Steelers ' leading receiver against Indianapolis, with five grabs for 81 yards.

The Steelers are already without No. 2 wideout Michael Pittman Jr., whose foot injury landed him on the injured reserve for the next four weeks, at least. If Wilson's injury is serious enough to sideline him for the rest of the matchup, Rodgers might have to lean on Brandon Smith, a practice squad call-up, and rookie returner Kaden Wetjen.

Ben Skowronek, another receiver, is questionable to return to the matchup with a leg injury, making the situation even more unclear.

articles.title: AC Milan maintain unbeaten record with draw at Sassuolo
articles.summary: AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 1-1 draw against Sassuolo on Sunday. Adrien Rabiot’s second half opener was cancelled out by Cas Oden...
articles.body:
AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 1-1 draw against Sassuolo on Sunday.

Adrien Rabiot's second half opener was cancelled out by Cas Odenthal just five minutes later as Milan settled for a point which keeps them fifth in the standings having won three and drawn three league games so far.

The hosts had early opportunities through Darryl Bakola and Domenico Berardi as they looked to break the deadlock in the opening stages.

Both teams suffered injury blows early in the match as Matteo Gabbia was forced off for Milan and just six minutes later fellow defender Fedde Leysen was unable to continue for Sassuolo.

Rabiot nodded over the crossbar for Milan and the visitors had a flurry of chances towards the end of the half when Gonçalo Ramos had two shots saved by Arijanet Muric.

The Sassuolo goalkeeper was called into action again during first half stoppage-time, stopping Diego Moreira's strike and Strahinja Pavlovic's header.

Vasilije Adzic went close after the restart when his close-range effort was saved by Mike Maignan, but Milan eventually broke the deadlock in the 63rd minute.

Substitute Luka Modrić threaded a pass into Rabiot on the left side of the box and the French midfielder hit a thumping strike past Muric.

However, Sassuolo piled on the pressure with Kieron Bowie and Kristian Thorstvedt testing Maignan in quick succession before Odenthal levelled in the 68th minute, hooking the ball home from a corner.

Shortly after the equalizer Samuel Chukwueze was denied by Muric, but the game fizzled out into a draw.

articles.title: Steelers lead Colts 17-13 at halftime
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers threw two touchdown passes, and the Steelers added Chris Boswell's 48-yard field goal late in the first half to take a 17-13 lead into the lock...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers threw two touchdown passes, and the Steelers added Chris Boswell's 48-yard field goal late in the first half to take a 17-13 lead into the locker room at halftime.

Rodgers threw scoring tosses of 80 yards to running back Jaylen Warren and 1 yard to tight end Pat Freiermuth. The first one was the 580th of his career, including the postseason, and allowed Rodgers to pass Peyton Manning for third on the all-time list.

Rodgers is 16-of-21 for 166 yards and a 130.3 passer rating.

The Steelers outgained the Colts 206 to 147 yards in the first half.

Warren had five catches for 81 yards and a touchdown and four carries for 13 yards.

Colts quarterback Daniel Jones went 10-of-15 for 132 yards. Jonathan Taylor had eight carries for 13 yards, and tight end Tyler Warren ran for a 1-yard touchdown on fourth down.

Josh Downs has two catches for 42 yards.

articles.title: Florida football knocked out of US LBM Top 25
articles.summary: Florida football is no longer in the US LBM Top 25 coaches poll after a 38-19 loss to South Carolina on homecoming.
articles.body:
Florida football was knocked out of the US LBM college football coaches poll after its 38-19 loss to South Carolina on homecoming on October 10.

The Florida Gators (4-2, 2-2 SEC) were ranked as high as No. 8 following an upset win over Ole Miss to close September 4-0, but have since dropped back-to-back games to Missouri and South Carolina by an average margin of 23.5 points.

The Gators were ranked No. 15 last week leading up to the South Carolina game.

"We clearly haven't arrived the last two weeks because we've been exposed in a pretty substantial way," Florida coach Jon Sumrall said. "And this conference will do it to you. But I think sometimes, and I said this last week as well, sometimes when you're winning, it masks maybe the things that are not going right or that you're not doing well."

UF is receiving 32 votes in the poll behind James Madison, coached by former Florida coach Billy Napier, who is receiving 33 votes.

Florida will look to regroup when it plays at No. 6 Texas on October 17 (noon, ABC). The Longhorns are coming off a 27-24 upset loss to rival Oklahoma, in which starting quarterback Arch Manning threw a pair of crucial interceptions.

Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun's Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Follow him on X @KevinBrockwayG1.

articles.title: Georgia takes over for Texas as CFP top seed based on AP Top 25; Longhorns would host 1st-round game
articles.summary: Georgia would replace Texas as the top seed on the 12-team College Football Playoff bracket based on The Associated Press Top 25 released Sunday, but the Lon...
articles.body:
Georgia would replace Texas as the top seed on the 12-team College Football Playoff bracket based on The Associated Press Top 25 released Sunday, but the Longhorns would still play at home in the first round.

The projected bracket underwent minor changes with Texas' loss to unranked Oklahoma knocking the Longhorns out of a top-four seed and the first-round bye that goes with it.

Georgia, Notre Dame, Miami each moved up one seed line from last week, Ohio State moves in at No. 4, and Indiana, Alabama, Texas and BYU would host first-round games.

The five highest-ranked conference champions — from the Power Four and one from the Group of Six — will qualify for the CFP. The other seven spots will be filled by the next highest-ranked teams. One of those at-large teams will be Notre Dame if the Fighting Irish are among the top 12 in the CFP's final rankings.

The Southeastern Conference would have four teams in the bracket, one less than last week because LSU dropped off following its loss to Kentucky . Utah replaced LSU and would give the Big 12 a third team in the tournament. The Big Ten would have two teams and the Atlantic Coast Conference and Pac-12 would have one each. Notre Dame would be in as an independent and Boise State would represent the Pac-12 as the top Group of Six champion.

Based on the AP rankings, the CFP would open like this:

No. 9 seed Mississippi at No. 8 BYU. Winner vs. No. 1 Georgia.

No. 12 seed Boise State at No. 5 seed Indiana. Winner vs. No. 4 Ohio State.

No. 10 seed Texas Tech at No. 7 Texas. Winner vs. No. 2 Notre Dame.

No. 11 seed Utah at No. 6 Alabama. Winner vs. No. 3 Miami.

The first three teams outside the bracket: UCLA, Missouri and Tennessee. The Bruins are ranked No. 12 by the AP but would get bumped by Boise State, the highest-ranked Group of Six team.

First-round games are Dec. 18 and 19, quarterfinals Dec. 30 and Jan. 1, semifinals Jan. 14 and 15 and the championship game is Jan. 25 at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas.

The AP will publish brackets based on the weekly Top 25 until the CFP selection committee unveils its initial rankings Nov. 3.

articles.title: Commanders lead Giants 12-3 at halftime
articles.summary: The Giants used J.J.
articles.body:
The Giants used J.J. McCarthy on one play during the first quarter of Sunday's game in Washington and the rest of their offensive performance over the first 30 minutes of play will have some wondering if he should get a longer look.

That performance saw the Giants pick up 70 total yards of offense and it saw starting quarterback Jameis Winston lose a fumble on a sack by linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson late in the second quarter. Tim Settle recovered the ball and Drew Stevens's second field goal of the half made it a 12-3 Washington lead at the break.

Winston is 7-of-16 for 72 yards and he was sacked twice in wet conditions in the first half. McCarthy's one play was a pop pass that resulted in a five-yard loss, but it was wiped out by a Commanders facemask penalty.

The Giants haven't found any more success on the ground while Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has seven carries for 50 yards. One of those was a 33-yard touchdown to cap the first possession of the game, but Stevens missed the extra point.

Jayden Daniels had two completions for 34 yards on the scoring drive and he's 6-of-11 for 85 yards in his first action since dislocating his left elbow in Week 2. He's also run five times and been sacked twice without showing any sign of issues with the elbow.

articles.title: Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey’s bold move that unlocked game-winning play to beat LSU
articles.summary: The Kentucky Wildcats pulled off a huge 35-34 upset win over the LSU Tigers on Saturday. It came to an end after quarterback Kenny Minchey ran it right up th...
articles.body:
The Kentucky Wildcats pulled off a huge 35-34 upset win over the LSU Tigers on Saturday. It came to an end after quarterback Kenny Minchey ran it right up the middle on a QB draw play to clinch the win on a game-winning two-point conversion. But how did that bold call come to fruition? It turns out it was Minchey's decision from the get-go.

Kentucky head coach Will Stein revealed that the initial call for the two-point conversion was not a designed QB draw , according to Big Blue Rando. While it was an incredibly bold decision, Stein is happy his transfer redshirt junior signal-caller made the call.

"We didn't call a QB draw," Stein admitted during the postgame press conference. "Kenny called his own number, and thank God he did."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Minchey had himself a game against LSU. Although he did not throw a single touchdown pass, he still totaled 246 passing yards with no interceptions while completing 63.8% of his pass attempts. He also ran in a touchdown on top of his two-point rushing score to seal the victory for Kentucky.

The Wildcats landed the 21-year-old quarterback in the transfer portal in the offseason. He joined Stein's program after playing for the Notre Dame Fighting Irish the previous three seasons. However, Minchey was a backup during his time in Marcus Freeman's offense, appearing in 10 total games over three years.

Kentucky will move on to Week 7 with a 5-1 record. The program is scheduled to take on the Oklahoma Sooners on the road next.

articles.title: Bobby Bowden’s football philosophy speaks volumes about FSU’s problems
articles.summary: After a tough loss to Louisville, FSU football faces questions about its identity and future under Mike Norvell.
articles.body:
The legendary Florida State coach won two national championships while believing that schemes mattered far less than the players entrusted to execute them. And when they failed to execute, Bowden didn't simply blame the players. Coaches had to coach better.

One can only imagine what Bowden would have thought watching his beloved Seminoles at Louisville on Friday night - and over the past few seasons under embattled seventh-year coach Mike Norvell.

There surely has been a few heavenly "dad-gums."

What on earth has happened to FSU football?

It's more about questioning FSU's direction than criticizing it

Honestly, this isn't about piling more criticism on Norvell. It's about examining the Seminoles ' troubling lack of fundamentals, cohesion and identity, and trying to determine why those problems continue to surface on game days.

Just when FSU fans had reason to feel good about their team after an impressive win over Virginia, Louisville happened. The Seminoles squandered a 14-0 lead, came one play from going ahead 21-0 and instead lost 44-20.

As a result, FSU saw its modest two-game win streak snapped and it now has lost 11 straight true road games and 13 straight away from Doak Campbell Stadium heading into Saturday's ACC rivalry game against No. 3 Miami.

Now FSU fans are left hoping for the best and waiting for answers, both on the field and from an administration considering changes that could reshape Seminoles athletics and the football program.

Norvell is 3-3 this season and 41-37 overall, with the high point coming during FSU's undefeated regular season and ACC championship run in 2023. Since then, little has gone right, and the frustration and anger among Seminoles fans have only intensified.

Still, FSU would prefer not to fire Norvell during the year.

As for structural changes within athletics that are expected to take shape soon, university board chair Peter Collins told the Tallahassee Democrat Tuesday, Sept. 29, in an exclusive interview that he's working in "lockstep" with President Richard McCullough to drive the changes that include hiring a new athletic director and bringing in other senior positions in athletics.

Louisville defeat difficult to forgive after blowing 14-0 lead

The Louisville loss remains difficult to shake, particularly after the encouraging win over Virginia.

FSU appeared poised to take a 21-0 lead early in the second quarter when it faced fourth-and-goal from the Louisville 3. But a slow-developing screen pass to freshman receiver Jasen Lopez was stopped at the 3, a pivotal moment in a game that soon turned dramatically.

Personally, I did not have an issue with Norvell's decision to go for it on fourth down. Norvell's aggressiveness in those situations has long been part of his coaching personality. The puzzling part was the play itself, especially with FSU running the football so effectively. Norvell defended the "thought process" behind it afterward without explaining exactly what that thought process was.

The Cardinals outgained the Seminoles 438-190 and outscored them 44-6 after the fourth-down stop.

FSU's defense, meanwhile, couldn't stop much of anything. Isaac Brown ran for a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on just 17 carries, including a game-changing 97-yard score after his team's defensive stop.

One can point to FSU's defensive problems under Tony White with alignment, run fits, edge containment and communication in the secondary. Those are basic responsibilities that should remain sound regardless of scheme or personnel. This is also about fundamentals, and I am not sure why it felt like there was always somebody out of place.

What would Bobby Bowden say about today's FSU football team?

Bowden Legacy Auction now live, take a look at items available

Nobody pretends to know exactly how FSU football reached this point. Fans simply know what they saw at Louisville, and what they have seen far too often the past two seasons.

Missed fits. Poor containment. Confusion. A team that, at times, looks disconnected from itself and reacts poorly to adversity.

Maybe the answer ultimately involves changes at the top or on the coaching staff. Maybe it runs deeper than that.

Bobby Bowden always preached "players, not plays," but that philosophy carried another responsibility: Put those players in position to succeed.

Since 2023, FSU simply hasn't done that consistently.

And until it does, the most troubling question will remain the simplest one: What exactly is missing?

Jim Henry is the award-winning sports editor at the Tallahassee Democrat and can be reached at jjhenry@tallahassee.com. Jim also co-authored "Tarnished Heisman," a 2008 book on Reggie Bush's career at USC.

articles.title: College Fantasy Football Waiver Wire, Week 7: Bear Bachmeier, Jaziun Patterson among top pickups
articles.summary: Eric Froton takes you through his top players to add off the college fantasy football waiver wire going into Week 7.
articles.body:
Week 6 was the second-most consequential bye week of the college football season, leaving the potential of some valuable open bench spots as players acquired for a spot start can be dropped in favor of higher-upside options who can help teams in the second half of the regular season. Here are some players who you should consider adding for the stretch run who are still available in most leagues.

Bear Bachmeier, BYU - 17% Rostered on Yahoo

A rock-solid asset whose husky, powerful frame makes him a goal-line vulture, Bachmeier has scored 29+ points in three-of-five games and cleared 20+ in four of them. Only a 7.78-point aberration against Colorado State blemishes an otherwise sterling résumé, with Bear averaging 24.4 PPG on the year. His rushing utility is key, as his 239 yards and four touchdowns on the ground give him an exceptionally high floor. He has zeroed in on true freshman WR Legend Glasker as his primary target, providing a downfield element to his game. Glasker is averaging a 17.4 ADOT on his targets, which is more than twice as much as the next highest ADOT on the team (TE Walker Lyons, 8.1). Which makes sense since BYU throws to the slot at the fourth-highest rate in the nation, emphasizing precision and staying on schedule as is evidenced by BYU's 53% success rate (5th in FBS). The one caveat is Notre Dame comes to Provo this weekend, so if you can stash Bachmeier on your bench, he's going to be a valuable asset against his second-half Big 12 slate.

Lopez was coming off 45.4 points against Stanford, and then had a 31.1-point eruption in a 38-14 bashing of NC State in Week 6. He should make it three big games in a row this weekend against a reeling Cal team that ranks 120th in pass plays of 20+ yards (19%).

If you're looking for week-in, week-out consistency, Fifita is as valuable as any QB in the country, scoring at least 21+ points in all six games, ranking sixth in QB points while averaging a cool 26.6 PPG. He's on bye this week, but has a dream matchup against Iowa State in Week 8 if you can float the bench spot for a week.

Jaziun Patterson, Michigan State - 5% Rostered

Injuries are out of our control, all we can do is adjust to the circumstances. When MSU RB1 Cam Edwards was lost for the season, Iowa transfer RB Jaziun Patterson was handed the reins to the starting running back job heading into last week's contest against Wisconsin. He rushed 18 times for 62 yards in a humiliating 31-3 loss to Illinois. This week, the Spartans were ready for Illinois, taking the game to OT in a heartbreaking 38-37 loss. Patterson was ready for the challenge as well, rushing 17 times for 93 yards and three touchdowns while catching three passes for 26 yards and another score for a gaudy 37.4 points. What was encouraging was just four carries were distributed to the rest of the RB room, which affirms the stranglehold Patterson has on the RB1 role. MSU had played a brutal set of run defenses prior to Illinois, and face a gauntlet of Big Ten contenders down the stretch, but Patterson is highly streamable against Northwestern in Week 7 .

After receiving just 16 carries for 108 yards over Notre Dame's first four games, the true freshman has amassed 36 carries for 301 yards and two touchdowns, with four receptions for 56 yards for 54.7 points over his last two contests. Walton has outscored his backfield contemporaries over the last two, solidifying a share of this rapidly evolving three-way dance between him, Aneyas Williams and Nolan James Jr. While it may be difficult to parse which player is going to go off each week, Notre Dame's schedule is so light it might not matter if they're all scoring 15+ points like they did in Week 6 against Stanford. Walton is a pickup and hold versus BYU on the road on Week 7.

Cardae Mack, Arizona State - 0% Rostered

I had been hearing about freshman sensation Cardae Mack since talking to my ASU sources who speculated that he could take the starting gig at some point this season. Despite his undeniable talent, Mack was not prominently featured in the spring depth chart. His time came this weekend while celebrating his 19th birthday with 13 carries for 154 yards and two touchdowns versus Hawaii, putting RB1 Kyson Brown on notice. Mack is an excellent bench stash to watch in the second half.

Ijeboi exploded on the scene with three straight games of 17+ points to open the season, including a 36.6-point bludgeoning of Wake Forest. Yet, he somehow slipped in roster rate after a forgivable 5.7-point performance against a superior Notre Dame defense and 8.0 points on 20 touches in a 24-17 victory over Illinois in Week 5. These minor hiccups are in the past after Ijeboi detonated on Minnesota, carving up the Gophers for 31 carries, 195 rushing yards, three touchdowns and 43.1 fantasy points in the 41-13 win. He needs to be active for his Week 7 contest against the hapless Washington Huskies.

With projected WR1 Tre Spivey and WR2 Giovanni Richardson both missing extended time, there were questions about which wideout would step up to become Fifita's new primary target. Despite making his first career start, Mizell answered the call with six catches for 183 yards and two touchdowns for 30.3 points in Week 6 against West Virginia. He had been a steady presence in the offense before getting the starting nod, earning 5+ targets in each of the last three games with two touchdown receptions in that span, so that breakout wasn't completely out of the blue. Head coach Brent Brennan praised Mizell's approach and preparation heading into the contest and he appears primed to take over the Arizona WR1 role after their Week 7 bye, when the Wildcats get to feast on Iowa State's secondary that ranks 126th in yards per successful pass (17.0).

"Cactus" Jack Foley, Wake Forest - 0% Rostered

With gawd as my witness, "Cactus" Jack Foley has broken NC State's secondary in half!

Few freshman wideouts have had the kind of impact that we've seen from Mrs. Foley's baby boy, with Cactus Jack benefitting from the extra attention NC State gave star Wake Forest WR Carlos Hernandez, reeling in eight catches for 156 yards and a touchdown for a career-high 24.4 points. It marks the third time in four games that Foley has eclipsed 50+ yards with a receiving touchdown as Wake Forest's offense continues to throttle its overmatched opponents. The Demon Deacons have scored 30+ points in five-of-six games, with their 33-20 loss to last year's National Championship runner-up, Miami. It's hard to believe he's still practically un-rostered despite being a key contributor in the expertly-schemed Wake Forest passing attack, which features just 12% of the pass attempts being contested. Foley is well worth starting if you need a bye-week WR against Cal in Week 7.

Mosley missed the last three games to injury, accounting for the surprisingly low 25% roster rate. He is now officially back after a 22.5-point explosion against Penn State this weekend and is an absolute matchup-proof superstar who should be everyone's priority on the waiver wire this week. His Week 7 bye is irrelevant, as Mosley is one of the top-15 fantasy wideouts in the country when healthy and a superstar in the making.

Glasker is the third true freshman wideout highlighted in this week's waiver column, with the budding star scorching Iowa State's secondary for a 75-yard touchdown reception and 19.9 points as BYU rolled up 506 total yards on a beleaguered ISU defense. It marks the fourth time in five games that Glasker produced 80+ total yards, as he is a dangerous weapon in the run game as well, recording 11 carries for 83 yards and two rushing scores. He is well worth scooping and holding for the rest of the season.

Syracuse has been a fantasy honey-hole for tight ends in recent years, with "TEITO" Oronde Gadsden II posting league-winning numbers and TE Dan Villari running Wildcat QB packages. The new beneficiary of the 'Cuse TE legacy is Bacheyie, who has somehow flown under the radar at a 1% roster rate despite catching a pass in four out of five games. He blew up for four receptions, 97 yards and a touchdown for a career-high 17.7 points in a close 28-25 loss to UVA this weekend. The fact Syracuse's defense frequently puts the offense in an aggressive pass script greatly favors Bacheyie despite the fact Syracuse has started three different quarterbacks in the last three weeks. He is an excellent start Week 7 against a Louisville defense that has been uncharacteristically soft this season.

Preston Douglas, NC State - 35% Rostered

Douglas has taken over Justin Joly's high-volume TE1 role for the Wolfpack and has parlayed it into one of the safer bets at the tight end position. Douglas has scored at least 7.0 points per game in every game this year, while securing at least four passes in each of the last four games. If you can stash Douglas on the bench for his Week 7 bye, he will be an auto-start Week 8 versus the pitiful Stanford defense.

articles.title: Kings center Maxime Raynaud injures patella in right knee and will be reevaluated in about two weeks
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud received some encouraging news from imaging on his injured right knee that showed a patellar subl...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud received some encouraging news from imaging on his injured right knee that showed a patellar subluxation and not anything far more serious that might jeopardize his season before it begins.

The Kings said Sunday their second-year big man would be reevaluated again in about two weeks.

Raynaud underwent an MRI exam late Saturday after going down with 2:32 left in the second quarter of a 111-106 preseason loss to Golden State when he collided with Stephen Curry as he was making a screen on the Warriors star.

"Being around the sport for pretty much my whole life, injuries are just hard, but they're part of what we do," Kings coach Doug Christie said after the game. "We care about each other on a deeper level than just teammates and coach and player, as I told him on the floor: 'I love you, man. We're here for you. We got you.' You don't want to hear that in those moments, but it's part of what we do. Unfortunately, we put ourselves at risk, but yeah, it's never a good thing."

Raynaud was on his back and clearly in pain as medical staff examined him on the floor at Chase Center. He eventually was helped up and moved into a wheelchair to leave the court for the locker room.

Kings general manager Scott Perry was positive afterward, saying, "he'll be back." Perry escorted the 7-foot-1 Raynaud off the court, and team owner Vivek Ranadive came by to check on Raynaud outside the locker room.

Raynaud later received a goodbye hug from Perry and left the locker room on crutches, an ice bag wrapped around the knee. He was in good spirits and smiling while walking out of Chase Center.

Raynaud had set a screen on Curry — who also went down after the collision — for teammate Darius Acuff and Raynaud immediately screamed and grabbed at his right knee.

He made all three of his field-goal attempts, including a 3-pointer, and three free throws for 10 points to go with five rebounds, an assist and one blocked shot in just less than nine minutes of action.

The Kings selected Raynaud 42nd overall in the second round of last year's draft, and the 23-year-old from France averaged 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.4 assists over 74 games as a rookie.

articles.title: Georgia football claims top spot, Texas falls in SEC Power Rankings | Goodbread
articles.summary: Georgia is the class of the SEC for now, after beating Alabama and claiming the top spot in the SEC power rankings. But how far did Texas fall?
articles.body:

Meanwhile, LSU caught its second loss at the hands of an upstart Kentucky team. And what's happened to Florida the last two weeks, anyway? Onto the rankings!

What to know : In our best Dennis Green voice: "You want to crown them? Crown them. They're exactly who we thought they were." Yes we do, and yes they are.

What to know : Moving up to No. 2 after a loss to Georgia? What, you thought a loss to Oklahoma would only drop the Longhorns to No. 2?

What to know : If the OU offense ruins this Sooners season, at least hats can be hung on a win over Texas.

What to know : If the Lane Kiffin-LSU honeymoon isn't over, the bill is at least coming due .

What to know : Perfect September, perfectly awful October.

What to know : If Alabama's offense could only score 17 at home against the Dawgs, what will Auburn score in Athens ?

What to know : A win over Florida and an upcoming open week means the Shane Beamer Survival Tour rolls on.

What to know : Mike Elko insulting the most popular Aggies message board with a 3-3 record is not the recipe for good will.

What to know : After a blowout loss to Ole Miss, I'm calling it − for the first time since 2023, this is indeed your father's Vanderbilt again.

What to know : A trip to Nashville gives the Razorbacks a legit chance to climb out of the cellar here.

articles.title: Toto Wolff’s Strict Transparency Rule Keeps Mercedes United
articles.summary: Toto Wolff revealed the secret to keeping Mercedes F1 united: absolute transparency. He learned this lesson from a bitter rivalry with Alain Prost.
articles.body:
The secret to keeping the Mercedes Formula 1 team from falling apart is not fancy contracts or big bonuses. It is a strict rule of total honesty between drivers. Team principal Toto Wolff insists on absolute transparency to stop the mistrust that destroys championship squads. This approach stems from a painful lesson he learned early in his career regarding the bitter rivalry between Alain Prost and Ayrton Senna.

Wolff admits he once did not understand why two great drivers would turn on each other. He asked Prost directly about the collapse of their partnership at McLaren. The answer was simple: the drivers never knew if the team favored one over the other. That lack of clarity created a toxic dynamic where every teammate felt like an enemy. Wolff now ensures his drivers know exactly where they stand at all times.

Wolff first asked these questions when he was a young executive at the Williams team. He wanted to know how the situation between Prost and Senna got so bad so quickly. He recalled asking Prost, according to Motorsport.com , "I said to him, I saw it on TV the whole thing, and I said how did that escalate between the two of you almost in a naive way, because I didn't understand the dynamics between the two drivers."

According to reports, the fundamental problem stemmed from the pitwall's total failure to provide transparency about equal status. Wolff recounted the conversation, noting that Prost felt uncertain about his position relative to his teammate. "He said the problem was that you never knew whether you were favoured," Wolff said. This uncertainty created a dynamic of mistrust within the team, leading to a feeling that a direct opponent might be given advantages.

Wolff realized that modern drivers often start their careers as scared children in go-karts. They spend their formative years relying on individual survival instincts in high-pressure series. To prevent the same toxicity, he established a rule of absolute honesty inside the Mercedes garage. Drivers cannot hide behind vague promises or secret deals.

This strict management style is vital right now as the team faces internal pressure. Andrea Kimi Antonelli is rapidly approaching the 2026 world drivers' championship title. At the same time, veteran George Russell is battling through relentless grid penalties on the other side of the garage. The internal dynamics could easily fracture under such intense pressure.

Wolff believes a team principal must provide a secure, balanced psychological environment. He knows that favouritism is the enemy of a winning team. By removing the mystery, he stops drivers from guessing who has the boss's ear. This prevents the "us versus them" mentality that can ruin a season before it even starts.

The result is a garage culture built on equal treatment. Wolff refuses to play the usual paddock politics. He insists that both drivers have access to the same information and resources. This approach keeps the focus on performance rather than office drama.

The strategy is working even when the weekend goes wrong. The 2026 Singapore Grand Prix showed just how hard racing can be on street tracks. George Russell started 19th on the grid after a massive 60-place penalty for new engine parts. He fought his way back but struggled to pass cars in front of him.

Wolff explained the difficulty of overtaking in those tight conditions. "Yeah, it's so difficult to overtake. I mean, he pulled off some really great moves," Wolff said, according to Motorsport.com . He observed that even a vehicle lagging by a second or a second and a half struggles to overtake easily. The lack of long straights makes it nearly impossible to get clean air.

While Russell faced a tough race, his teammate Antonelli secured a podium finish. This success proved that the team's new aerodynamic upgrades are working as intended. The hard-fought result showed that the technical team has solved its balance issues. It also showed that the drivers can perform when the car is competitive.

Max Verstappen also had a breakthrough weekend, winning his second consecutive race. He ended a long curse of finishing second at the Marina Bay Street Circuit. "Yeah. It's taken a while," Verstappen said after his win, according to Motorsport.com . His success has given Red Bull a boost in motivation after a season dominated by Mercedes.

For Mercedes, the focus remains on keeping the garage united. Wolff knows that without trust, even the fastest car will fail. The strict transparency is not just a policy; it is the foundation of their survival. As the season continues, this rule will decide if they can hold off the challenge from Red Bull.

articles.title: Chargers' keys to victory against the Broncos
articles.summary: Here's what the Los Angeles Chargers need to do to win in Week 5.
articles.body:
The Chargers host the Broncos on Sunday in a game between the bottom two teams in the AFC West, with both squads entering the weekend with the panic meters nearing their upper limits.

Here's what Los Angeles needs to do to get its first win of the year.

Denver's linebackers have long been the weakness of their unit in both phases on defense, but the Broncos have yet to address their personnel on the second level of the defense. Until they do, the easiest way to beat Denver will be to force Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad to do as much as possible. In the ground game, that likely means focusing more on combo blocks on defensive linemen and getting into space to let the Broncos linebackers make mistakes and open holes on their own. Through the air, this may be an ideal game to get tight end Oronde Gadsden II more involved - his career debut resulted in 5 catches for 46 yards against the Broncos in Week 3 last season.

Cornerbacks Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss will miss Sunday's game, leaving Denver with nickel Ja'Quan McMillian, 2025 first-rounder Jahdae Barron, and Kris Abrams-Draine as the only healthy corners. Denver also has undrafted rookie Brent Austin and return specialist Sean Fresch Jr. on the practice squad. That's a far cry from one of the top corner duos in the league and a former Defensive Player of the Year on the back end.

There's a realistic world where Los Angeles has to start four rookies - second-rounder Jake Slaughter, fourth-rounder Travis Burke, sixth-rounder Logan Taylor, and undrafted free agent Jacob Spomer - alongside Cole Strange, with sixth-rounder Alex Harkey, Branson Taylor and practice squad players as depth. Against a Denver defensive front that includes Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, the Chargers will need to scheme around a unit that will be learning on the job for virtually the entire game.

Over the past four weeks, the main problem with the Chargers' offense appears to be that they're not leaning into the things that made them successful. Justin Herbert has struggled on the predetermined anticipation throws offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was known for in Miami and the run game has gotten predictable with Keaton Mitchell essentially only entering the game when LA plans to run outside the tackles. The second half against Seattle showed glimpses of what the Chargers offense can be if they find a groove: Herbert threw more straight dropback read concepts and Omarion Hampton found running room between the tackles on more gap-focused runs. If those are major parts of the offense this week and beyond, the Chargers might be able to turn a corner.

Denver is switching up their offensive structure this week, moving playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb back to head coach Sean Payton after a four-week trial for Webb that resulted in the 23rd-ranked offense by EPA/play. It's unclear, however, how Payton and Webb have split game-planning duties this week and who will be the voice in quarterback Bo Nix's ear on Sunday. Los Angeles has an opportunity to capitalize on that uncertainty and keep the Broncos' offensive struggles in the news beyond Sunday afternoon.

Nix has the sixth-lowest depth of target on his passes this season, ahead of only Cooper Rush, Daniel Jones, Jalon Daniels, Deshaun Watson, and Tyson Bagent. Denver's run game has also not been able to get much momentum going - they have the fourth-lowest rushing yards per game this season - so if the Chargers are able to control the line of scrimmage and keep Denver behind the sticks, they should be able to get the Broncos off the field at a decent clip and give the Chargers offense more opportunities to succeed.

Nix has the third-lowest pressure to sack ratio of any quarterback this season, behind only Brock Purdy and Jayden Daniels, but has thrown the ball faster than either of those passers on average this season. Denver has frequently checked the ball down, sometimes before allowing downfield routes to develop, seemingly because Nix is feeling pressure - his 58 pressured dropbacks are tied for 11th-most in the league this season. Chargers edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack have 14 pressures apiece this season, so if they can constrict the pocket and make Nix feel distressed, they may not even need to finish plays for their presence to result in positive outcomes for Los Angeles.

Derwin James and Donte Jackson are out for this game. If Denver gets more aggressive with Payton calling plays, LA will need to find ways to direct attention away from their corners and let safeties Elijah Molden, Tony Jefferson, Genesis Smith, and RJ Mickens carry the secondary instead.
