articles.title: Steve Sarkisian won't change play-calling duties, special teams coach after Oklahoma loss
articles.summary: After a 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, Steve Sarkisian was asked if he'd give up being UT's offensive playcalling or change who coaches the Longhorns on special tea...
articles.body:
DALLAS – Following a 27-24 loss Saturday to Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl, two questions and two answers from Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian 's postgame media conference were noteworthy.

After the top-ranked team in the Associated Poll struggled offensively in a setback that was decided by Tate Sandell's 47-yard field goal as time expired, would Sarkisian give up his playcalling duties?

"Not a chance," Sarkisian bluntly stated.

And would Texas consider changing the duties of special teams coordinator Jeff Banks after disastrous showings against Tennessee and Oklahoma?

Sarkisian's answers weren't necessarily surprising. Last year, he rebuffed calls to cede his play-calling responsibilities and argued that "That's why I got hired (by Texas). I was a really good offensive coordinator." Banks has also worked with Sarkisian since both coaches were assistants at Alabama in 2019.

So the important takeaway may not be why Sarkisian answered those questions in the manner that he did on Saturday. The important takeaway may be why two Texas beat reporters - CJ Vogel of On Texas Football and Thomas Jones of the Austin American-Statesman - needed to ask those questions in the first place.

Texas lacks offensive consistency in Sooners setback

Texas (4-1, 1-1) has scored 157 points this season, but 37.6% of those points were scored in the team's season opener against Texas State. The Longhorns scored 24 and 20 points in its close wins over Ohio State and Tennessee, and UT struggled against another Power Four-level defense on Saturday.

Oklahoma (3-2, 1-1) entered Saturday with a creditable defense, and the Longhorns were unable to make the case that reputation wasn't deserved. Oklahoma returned one of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 's fourth-quarterback interceptions into the end zone, and the other turnover set up Sandell's game-winning kick.

Texas did put together four scoring drives against Oklahoma. However, the Longhorns' other 11 possessions went nowhere:

seven plays, 38 yards (missed field goal)

As a result, Texas failed to score 30 points against Oklahoma for the second straight season. The Longhorns had averaged 40.3 points during Sarkisian's first four Red River Rivalry games.

"I think there's a ton of belief in what we're doing," Sarkisian said. "I think you saw some of the explosive playmaking ability that we can have on this offense, but we've got to find a level of consistency. My job is to figure that out."

Said Manning: "We've got to win on first and second down, make third down easier."

Texas can't get things going on special teams for a second straight week

But while UT's performance on offense was concerning, its effort on special teams may have best been described as alarming. Gianni Spetic booted the game-opening kickoff out of bounds and later missed a 53-yard field goal that would have given the Longhorns a late lead. Texas punt returner Ryan Niblett, who scored on a 75-yard return in last year's Red River Rivalry game, averaged 3.2 yards on Saturday's five returns.

Oklahoma's only points in the first half were scored when Mac Chiumento's blocked punt was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown. A touchdown off of a blocked punt had last been scored against Texas in 2009.

"We're better than that," Sarkisian said. "I've got to find a way to get our guys playing with more confidence from a specialist standpoint."

During the Longhorns' recent bye week, Sarkisian acknowledged that the Banks-led special teams needed to improve . Against Tennessee on Sept. 26, Texas allowed a punt-return touchdown for the first time since 2013, failed to recover an onside kick and had Spetic send a kickoff out of bounds.

Longhorns express optimism with Florida up next

Sarkisian wasn't the only Longhorn to offer a dissenting opinion to the media after the Longhorns' first loss of the season. When asked if Oklahoma was the better team at the Cotton Bowl, Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons replied "we definitely beat ourselves. Only Texas can beat Texas."

Simmons' defense only allowed 13 points on Saturday, but that side of the football was responsible for two key penalties on one Oklahoma touchdown drive and the Sooners did pick up 33 passing yards in a 16-second span as it set up the game's final kick. So in other words, there was plenty of blame to go around in the Texas locker room. And with Florida coming to Royal-Memorial Stadium this weekend, the Longhorns will have to address their issues immediately.

"There's a level of frustration, a level of disappointment, a level of anger but also a level of optimism knowing we can get these things fixed and we've got a long season to go," Sarkisian said. "We've got a good football team. We're not dead, we're going to be OK. We'll get back up off the mat."

Oklahoma receiver Parker Livingstone (3) celebrates after beating Texas in the Red River Rivalry game at the Cotton Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman)

articles.title: Florida drops out of AP Top 25 after South Carolina loss
articles.summary: Florida went from No. 8 to unranked in the AP Top 25 Poll over two weeks after back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina.
articles.body:
Florida 's second straight loss cost the Gators their spot in the AP Top 25 .

Florida dropped out of the rankings Sunday after a 38-19 home loss to South Carolina, completing a two-week fall from inside the top 10 to No. 16 and now out of the poll entirely. The Gators still received nine votes, leaving them seventh among teams outside the top 25.

The fall comes after Florida opened the season 4-0 and climbed as high as No. 8 following its win over Ole Miss. Back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina erased that momentum quickly, with the Gators now sitting at 4-2 overall and 2-2 in SEC play.

Florida was one of three teams to fall out of the poll this week, joining Oregon and Pittsburgh. Kentucky, Wake Forest and Northwestern entered the rankings, while Georgia moved to No. 1 after beating Alabama 20-17. Notre Dame climbed to No. 2, Miami remained No. 3 and Ohio State moved to No. 4.

Others receiving votes: Wisconsin 92, Oregon 86, Arizona 82, Nebraska 65, Oklahoma 44, James Madison 29, Florida 9, Duke 5, New Mexico 3, Oregon State 1

articles.title: David Montgomery knocked out with groin injury
articles.summary: Houston Texans running back David Montgomery left the Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans due to a groin injury, and he has been ruled out
articles.body:
Houston Texans running back David Montgomery (groin) left the Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans due to a groin injury, and he has been ruled out for the rest of the game.

Montgomery finished with five rushes for 11 yards, while he was not targeted in the passing game.

Why it Matters: With Montgomery sidelined, Woody Marks will be leaned upon as the primary ball carrier for the Texans down the stretch against Tennessee. Marks would have some RB3 or flex fantasy value if he is the top dog in the Houston backfield. Dare Ogunbowale could also see some snaps and backfield touches going forward, but his fantasy value remains rather negligible.
